kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "More about beach holidays on tours of Argentina and Brazil"
lead: >-
  On combined itineraries through Argentina and Brazil, beach days usually take place on the Brazilian coast: Praia de Pipa, Ilha Grande, Paraty, Búzios or Praia do Forte. The Argentine part introduces Buenos Aires, Iguazu Falls and sometimes Patagonia's glaciers. Choose an itinerary based on how many nights you want by the ocean and which beach you prefer, then plan the sightseeing portion.
---

## Where to relax by the ocean if you also want to see Argentina

**On most suitable itineraries, seaside relaxation takes place in Brazil, while Argentina adds cultural and natural experiences.** That is the key principle of this combination. Argentine cities, glaciers and waterfalls do not become beach resorts just because the catalog groups the two countries together.

A journey often starts in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and on the Argentine side of Iguazu Falls before continuing to Brazil's ocean coast. Other itineraries begin in Rio and leave the beach for the end. Both approaches make sense: after busy days of sightseeing and flying, a few quieter days by the sea are a chance to finish the journey without another long excursion.

Our selection offers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Argentina and Brazil as main countries and a significant beach element. Some complete itineraries also include other nations or optional excursions. For trips without this thematic filter, see [all routes through Argentina and Brazil](/multi-country/argentina_brazil/).

## Four ways to spend beach days in Brazil

### Praia de Pipa: ending the journey beside a warm ocean

[Praia de Pipa](/brazil/place/praia-de-pipa/) in northeastern Brazil suits an itinerary where, after Buenos Aires, Patagonia and Iguazu, you want a few days by the sea. Beaches here are bordered by sandy cliffs and green slopes; waves and swimming conditions differ along the coast.

The [11-day “Argentina and Brazil” tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/) connects Buenos Aires, El Calafate, Iguazu and Pipa. The Argentine stage focuses on the city and glaciers, while the Brazilian stage ends at the ocean. This is a clear example of “sightseeing first, beach at the end.”

### Ilha Grande and Paraty: bays, an island and a historic town

[Ilha Grande](/brazil/place/ilha-grande/) and [Paraty](/brazil/place/paraty/) lie south of Rio. Holidays here feature scenic bays, island beaches and walks through Paraty's historic center. It is not one continuous urban beach: some bays are reached by boat, and weather affects departures at sea.

The [12-day Brazil itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-sao-paulo-iguazu-rio-ilha-grande-paraty-12-days/) also visits the Argentine side of Iguazu and therefore appears in this combined-country selection. After São Paulo, the falls and Rio, days 8–11 are devoted to Ilha Grande, Paraty and Trindade. It suits travelers looking for beaches as well as small historic towns.

### Praia do Forte: several days on the northeastern coast

On the [14-day itinerary with Salvador and Iguazu](/multi-country/tour/brazil-rio-ouro-preto-salvador-praia-do-forte-iguazu-14-days/), days 7–10 take place around Praia do Forte. Before the beach, travelers visit Rio, Ouro Preto and Salvador, then return to sightseeing on both the Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazu.

Here the beach stop comes **before** the final waterfall visits. If you want a few days of complete relaxation just before your flight home, compare this order with the trip via Pipa.

### Búzios: peaceful days after Rio and Iguazu

The [private “Luxury Brazil” tour](/multi-country/tour/luxury-brazil/) includes Rio, Iguazu with a visit to the Argentine side, and several days in Búzios. This combination suits travelers who prefer a longer stay in one coastal town. The specific itinerary includes beach days without compulsory sightseeing every day.

The tour's name does not mean that every hotel or beach option is located in the same bay. Compare accommodation against the actual offer.

## Comparing itineraries by beach time

| Itinerary | Beach section | What comes before or after |
|---|---|---|
| Argentina and Brazil, 11 days | Praia de Pipa | Buenos Aires, Patagonia, Iguazu |
| São Paulo, Rio and the coast, 12 days | Ilha Grande, Paraty | São Paulo, Rio, Iguazu |
| Rio, Salvador and Iguazu, 14 days | Praia do Forte | Historic towns, two Iguazu parks |
| Private Brazil tour, 11 days | Búzios | Rio and both sides of Iguazu |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_argentina_brazil_pipa_11d,tour_brazil_sao_paulo_rio_ilha_paraty_12d,tour_brazil_gems_14d,tour_luxury_brazil_11d}}

Look beyond the overall duration. For example, the beach section of the 14-day program is concentrated in several overnight stays; the rest involves cultural excursions and internal transfers. The island option requires separate transport to Ilha Grande, while the trip via Pipa has a longer connection from Iguazu to the northeastern coast.

## Seasons, rainfall and different coastal conditions

Brazil extends a long way from north to south, so Pipa and Ilha Grande do not have identical seasonal weather. Check the local rainy season separately for the northeast coast; near Rio and Paraty, consider the likelihood of heavy rain in warmer months and conditions for boat departures.

Swimming conditions can differ between neighboring beaches: some have considerable surf, while other bays have calmer water, and tides can substantially change the width of the sand. When choosing accommodation, it helps to describe the experience you want—swimming in calm water, waves, walking or boat trips—rather than simply choosing a famous resort.

If the itinerary also includes [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), pack for two contrasting climates. A windproof jacket and warm layer are useful in Patagonia, while Brazil's coast calls for sun and rain protection. At [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), clothing and shoes should be suitable for wet walkways and spray.

## Should you leave the beach for the final days?

After an extensive sightseeing section, a few nights by the ocean allow time to recover before a long flight. This order is especially appealing when Buenos Aires, the glaciers and Iguazu come first. However, it can increase the risk of difficult connections if reaching the international airport from a beach town requires a long road transfer and a domestic flight.

For Ilha Grande, logistics depend on the crossing from the mainland; for Pipa, the transfer to Natal Airport matters. Avoid scheduling an international flight immediately after a long transfer without a sufficient buffer.

Visiting the Argentine side of Iguazu makes the journey international even when most nights are spent in Brazil. Travelers need documents for every planned border crossing. Tickets and visiting schedules for the Brazilian and Argentine national parks also need separate consideration.

## How Ada Tours combines sightseeing and beach holidays

When requesting a journey, tell us how many **full days** you would like to spend by the ocean without compulsory activities, how many transfers you are comfortable with, and which natural sights are essential. We then compare actual itineraries, transfer durations, accommodation types and excursion days. This helps you choose between an island, a historic coastal town, a resort near Pipa and the beaches of Búzios without unnecessary connections.

For a wider selection, explore [beach tours featuring Brazil](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/brazil/) and [all multi-country beach journeys](/multi-country/interests/beach-holidays/). Argentina remains a confirmed main country on the itineraries here, rather than an incidental optional outing.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does this combination include beach holidays in Argentina itself?

On the available itineraries described, the main beach section is on Brazil's coast. Argentine stops usually focus on Buenos Aires, Iguazu and sometimes Patagonia. Do not assume Argentine beaches are included unless the itinerary explicitly mentions them.

### Can I combine Perito Moreno Glacier and the beaches of Pipa in one trip?

Yes. The 11-day route through Buenos Aires, El Calafate, Iguazu and Praia de Pipa includes both. Domestic flights and clothing for cold and warm weather will be needed.

### Which is better for a beach holiday after Rio: Ilha Grande or Búzios?

Ilha Grande appeals for its island bays and boat excursions; Búzios allows you to stay in a coastal town with several beaches. The choice depends on transportation, hotel preferences and comfort with boat crossings.

### How many days are actually allocated to the beach?

It depends on the tour. Some have several beach days in a row; others offer only a short break between excursions. Check overnight stays and free days rather than the tour's overall length.

### Is it possible to skip Iguazu?

Iguazu is an important part of the international geography in the itineraries listed, but a different combination can be discussed when designing a custom tour. That would be a separate proposal, not a ready-made program from this selection.

targetPath: /multi-country/argentina_brazil/interests/culture-and-history/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "More about the culture of Argentina and Brazil"
lead: >-
  A journey through Argentina and Brazil brings together different urban traditions. Buenos Aires introduces tango, immigration history and the neighborhoods of the Río de la Plata; Rio de Janeiro offers Brazilian urban life and a cityscape between mountains and sea. Some tours add Salvador and the heritage of Portuguese Brazil. Choose by the actual excursions and time in each city: being listed together in the catalog does not guarantee equally rich cultural activities in both countries.
---

## What Argentina and Brazil offer on one cultural journey

**Argentina and Brazil have different languages, urban traditions and historical narratives, making their capital and coastal cities a particularly interesting combination.** In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the central squares, San Telmo, La Boca and Recoleta help explain how a city developed along the Río de la Plata. In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), historic buildings, theaters and public spaces coexist with Corcovado, Sugarloaf and beaches.

Tango emerged from the cultural environments of Buenos Aires and Montevideo; UNESCO inscribed the Argentine-Uruguayan tango tradition on its intangible heritage list in 2009. Brazil offers a different history: the Portuguese language, African cultural heritage, music and the architecture of colonial towns. These traditions are best compared through real excursions and encounters rather than a brief airport stop.

Our selection offers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Argentina and Brazil among the main countries and a significant culture-and-history component. **Some itineraries also visit Uruguay, Chile or Peru.** Two countries in the filter do not necessarily mean that the entire tour consists of just two countries. For an unrestricted geographic selection, see [all Argentina + Brazil routes](/multi-country/argentina_brazil/).

## Buenos Aires: neighborhoods, architecture and tango

On a cultural day in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), it is worth comparing several districts. **Plaza de Mayo and the Casa Rosada** are associated with Argentina's political history; San Telmo reveals old streets and urban commerce, while La Boca is known for colorful façades and its port history. Recoleta and Puerto Madero offer another architectural perspective.

The [10-day Argentina and Brazil tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-brazil-10-days/) begins in Buenos Aires, then travels via El Calafate and Iguazu Falls to Rio. Cultural activities focus primarily on the major cities. Perito Moreno Glacier enriches the journey as a natural experience, but visiting it should not be described as a historical excursion.

On the [13-day Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/), Buenos Aires is followed by an introduction to gaucho life on a ranch and then Colonia del Sacramento and Montevideo. The third country expands the colonial-history theme but requires more time and separate entry arrangements.

## Rio and Salvador: which cultural experiences are actually included

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), a sightseeing day may combine Corcovado, Sugarloaf and the historic center. UNESCO has recognized the cultural value of Rio's urban landscape between mountains and sea. It shows how nature has shaped architecture, city planning and everyday life. But a panorama from a viewpoint and an in-depth tour through old streets are different experiences.

On the [14-day itinerary from the Amazon to Argentina](/multi-country/tour/brazil-amazon-argentina-manaus-iguazu/), Rio is joined by Manaus and [Salvador](/brazil/place/salvador/). In Salvador, you explore Pelourinho and the historic center. This allows you to compare Buenos Aires with the former capital of Portuguese Brazil. UNESCO notes that Salvador served as Brazil's capital from 1549 to 1763 and became a meeting point of European, African and Indigenous American cultures.

Stops in the Amazon and on the beaches of Praia do Forte in the same tour expand its geography but should not automatically be counted as museum or ethnographic excursions. The Amazon itinerary separately includes an introduction to caboclo life and an evening on the river: a different experience from a historical walk in Salvador.

## Comparing the current cultural itineraries

| Program | Main emphasis |
|---|---|
| Argentina and Brazil, 10 days | Buenos Aires, Rio, Iguazu |
| Three countries, 13 days | Capitals, gauchos, Uruguay |
| Amazon and Salvador, 14 days | Rio, Pelourinho, Buenos Aires |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_argentina_and_brazil_ru,tour_source_stolitsy_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_source_tur_v_braziliyu_s_amazoniej_i_argentinu}}

**For a cultural journey, the number of full city days matters more than the length of the country list.** If tango interests you, leave time in Buenos Aires for an evening performance where one is actually included. If you want to explore Afro-Brazilian and colonial heritage, choose an itinerary with Salvador rather than just any tour that crosses Brazil.

Compare other options in [cultural tours featuring Argentina](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/) and [cultural tours featuring Brazil](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/). A country in these catalogs may be a primary or secondary destination, so check the specific days.

## Planning transfers so there is time for cities

On a two-country journey, the most common connection is the Iguazu area. Travelers may visit the [Brazilian side of the falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and the [Argentine side](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) before flying to Buenos Aires or Rio. These are separate nature excursions and an international border crossing; their duration cannot be counted as time spent on a cultural city walk.

Distinguish between EZE and AEP airports in Buenos Aires, and GIG and SDU in Rio. If a flight and city excursion fall on the same day, the entire hotel-to-hotel journey, baggage collection and transfer time matter. We help coordinate the sequence of stops, overland travel and excursion days while preserving time for the cultural portion.

Argentina and Brazil have different currencies, languages and immigration rules. Holding a second passport, traveling via a third country and making repeat entries call for individual checks. Travelers should confirm each excursion's content, guide language, admission tickets, free walking time and conditions for performances in advance. A tour's name is no substitute for a list of paid services.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural tours in Argentina and Brazil

### Can I experience tango and Brazilian culture in one trip?

Yes. Routes through Buenos Aires and Rio make that possible. Check the specific tour itinerary for tango shows and dedicated cultural excursions.

### Must I add Salvador to see historic Brazil?

No. Rio also offers substantial city excursions. Salvador adds a distinctive perspective on Portuguese colonial history and Afro-Brazilian heritage; it requires extra days and flights.

### Is an excursion to Iguazu part of the cultural program?

It is primarily a natural experience. A guide can explain the parks' historical context, but the falls do not replace excursions through Buenos Aires, Rio or Salvador.

### If the tour includes Uruguay or Chile, will every country have a cultural program?

Only if the itinerary specifies one. The thematic tag applies to the journey overall; an additional country may contribute a nature-focused, transit or beach stage.

### How should I choose between 10 and 14 days?

Compare the actual nights in the cities that interest you and the days spent traveling. A longer trip can add Salvador or the Amazon, but that is a different set of experiences, not automatically more time in Rio and Buenos Aires.

targetPath: /multi-country/argentina_brazil/interests/events-and-festivals/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "More about festival tours of Brazil and Argentina"
lead: >-
  Festival tours of Brazil and Argentina combine Carnival or New Year's Eve
  in Rio de Janeiro with Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires. The main event date
  is usually in Brazil: a visit to the Sambadrome or New Year's Eve on
  Copacabana Beach. Compare the Champions' Parade, regular Carnival days
  and New Year celebrations to find the right event.
---

## Carnival and New Year: which events are included in Brazil–Argentina tours?

The key question when choosing a festive trip to these two countries is: **which event in Rio de Janeiro do you want to attend?** Some programs focus on Carnival and the Sambadrome, others on the Champions' Parade, and still others on New Year's Eve at Copacabana. After Brazil, travelers head to [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), where tango shows and excursions through historic districts may be available.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Argentina and Brazil as main countries and the “Events and Festivals” theme. Combining countries **does not mean a festival is scheduled in both**: on most suitable itineraries, the main dated event takes place in Brazil, and the Argentine stage continues the journey after the celebration. Some tours also cover Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Read the full geography and festival itinerary for your selected product.

## Three festive scenarios that should not be confused

| Reason for traveling | What to check before choosing |
|---|---|
| Main Rio Carnival days | Exact Sambadrome date and included tickets |
| Champions' Parade | A ticket for the final procession of the winning samba schools |
| New Year on Copacabana | Night of December 31–January 1, hotel location and transportation after the celebration |

### Carnival at the Sambadrome

Carnival processions take place in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) on specific dates, and each day's program differs. Samba schools perform at the Sambadrome; spectators watch from the stands and the sections specified by their tickets. Walking along streets decorated for Carnival, visiting a samba school and attending the main parade are three distinct experiences. A tour title containing “Carnival” does not replace checking the ticket arrangements.

For instance, the [“Rio Carnival, Argentina and Iguazu” journey](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-rio-carnival-iguazu-10-days/) includes a Carnival evening in Rio, followed by the Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazu and Buenos Aires. Its current dates and ticket inclusions must be checked against the itinerary itself. Other tours may cover different Carnival days; if travel dates change, the organizer must reconfirm access to the intended parade.

### The 2027 Carnival Champions' Parade

The Champions' Parade is a separate event at which the best schools from the main competition return to the Sambadrome. **Rio's 2027 calendar schedules the Champions' Parade for February 13.** It is not held on the same date as the competitive parades; tickets and travel plans must match the intended evening.

The [10-day “Champions' Parade, Tango and Wine” program](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/) describes inclusion of the Champions' Parade and transfers between the hotel and Sambadrome. After Rio, the itinerary includes both sides of Iguazu, Buenos Aires with tango, and Santiago. This departure requires confirmation, so a published page alone must not be taken as a final reserved place in the stands.

There is also a longer [18-day five-country tour featuring the Champions' Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/), which continues after Brazil and Argentina through Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Choosing it means committing to an extensive journey across the Andes, not just a short holiday built around one evening.

### New Year in Rio de Janeiro

A different type of journey is being on Copacabana on the night of **December 31–January 1**. The [11-day New Year tour of Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/) lists December 30, 2026–January 9, 2027. New Year's Eve is spent on Copacabana, after which the route passes Iguazu and Buenos Aires before reaching Santiago. Being on the beach is not the same as having particular paid festive services included: dinner, a dedicated venue or a viewing position may need separate confirmation.

The [10-day New Year tour of Brazil and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-new-year-10-days/) is shorter and has no mandatory continuation into Chile. It also combines Rio during the celebrations, Iguazu and the Argentine capital. Travelers who want to devote more time to two countries may find it more convenient than an extensive multi-country itinerary.

## Which festive itineraries to compare

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_brazil_argentina_chile_champions_parade_10_days_2027,tour_source_mechty_sbyvayutsya_na_parad_chempionov_karnavala,tour_brazil_argentina_chile_new_year_11_days_2027,tour_source_mechty_sbyvayutsya_na_novyj_god}}

Each option has a focal event around which the entire schedule needs to be built. If you want **the Champions' Parade specifically**, your Rio stay must coincide with that evening. If the main Carnival competition matters more, select another Sambadrome date. If you dream of welcoming the new year by the ocean, late-December dates matter more than February events.

Also compare how far the itinerary continues after the celebration. The [nine-day Champions' Parade tour with Iguazu and Buenos Aires](/multi-country/tour/brazil-carnival-champions-parade-dreams/) offers a shorter continuation. Larger programs may involve several weeks traveling through South America, without necessarily including more festive events.

## Argentina after the festivities: waterfalls, tango and city breaks

A busy night in Rio is usually followed by a flight to Iguazu. The Brazilian side has panoramic walkways and expansive waterfall views. The Argentine side near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) offers a different experience of walking through a national park. If both sides are planned, allow time for crossing the border, park admission and the onward flight. Entering Argentina is a distinct logistical stage even if both parks are simply called “Iguazu.”

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), some tours include a tango show with dinner. This is a cultural event in its own right, but **it is not a separate Argentine carnival** and is often available outside the festival season. Check the specific package for tango, dinner and transfer inclusions: the word “tango” on different pages does not guarantee identical services.

For ordinary trips outside festival dates, see [all Argentina and Brazil tours](/multi-country/argentina_brazil/). If culture and city experiences are the main goal, compare a festive evening with a [Buenos Aires tango-show excursion](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-tango-show-with-dinner/) and decide what matters most for your trip.

## What to confirm before paying

**Sambadrome admission.** The date, type of parade, section, number of tickets and included transfers all matter. A night event may end very late; leave a realistic buffer before any flight the next morning.

**Hotels and festival nights.** During Carnival and New Year, Rio hotels may apply special conditions and minimum-stay restrictions. Requirements depend on the actual offer. For Copacabana, the hotel's location, access to the beach and the return trip after the celebrations matter just as much as a beautiful map view.

**Flights and borders.** Separate flights may be needed between [Rio](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). Entry documents must be checked for participants' citizenship and all countries on the full itinerary. Programs that include Chile or Bolivia add borders, time zones and expenses.

**Budget.** Comparing only starting prices is insufficient: check accommodation types, Sambadrome sections, festive dinners, guides and included transfers. Two tours named after the same event may differ substantially in their services.

## Frequently asked questions about festive tours of Brazil and Argentina

### Are the Champions' Parade and Rio's main Carnival the same event?

No. The Champions' Parade follows the main samba-school competition and has its own tickets and date. It is scheduled for February 13 in the 2027 calendar. Choose according to the specific evening and itinerary.

### Do all tours include a Sambadrome ticket?

No. Appearing in this thematic catalog indicates the tour has a festive focus, not that all tours include the same tickets. Check the itinerary for the exact events, sections and transfers in your selected package.

### Can I visit both sides of Iguazu after Carnival?

Yes, such itineraries are available. For example, the [Champions' Parade tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/) includes both Brazilian and Argentine national parks. Border-crossing time and a coordinated transfer sequence are required.

### Is there a festive event in Argentina on every such tour?

No. Argentina often contributes the falls and Buenos Aires with tango, while Carnival or New Year dates are tied to Rio. Tango shows are cultural evenings that may take place independently of the festivals.

### Which option is best for nine to eleven days?

For this duration, shorter “Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires” itineraries with a specific Carnival or New Year event are suitable. Adding Chile reduces free time in each country. Compare [all multi-country festival tours](/multi-country/interests/events-and-festivals/) as well.

lead: >-
  A gastronomic itinerary through Argentina and Brazil may combine Argentine
  wineries, a tango dinner in Buenos Aires, Rio de Janeiro and Iguazu Falls.
  But wine tastings are far from universal on two-country programs: some
  thematic tours visit wineries in Chile, which is part of the same itinerary.

---

## Argentina and Brazil: where wine appears and where city experiences take over

A trip through [Argentina](/argentina/) and [Brazil](/brazil/) offers several food-and-wine possibilities. You can spend several days visiting Argentine wineries, pair a tango dinner in Buenos Aires with exploring Rio, or continue to Chilean wine valleys. **These are different journeys.** Even when a tour is categorized as “Food and Wine,” look for an actual winery visit, tasting or substantial culinary day in its program.

Our selection offers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with both countries on the main route and a gastronomic theme. Some also pass through Chile or Uruguay. For example, a Maipo Valley tasting belongs specifically to the Chilean stage even if the tour is listed under “Argentina + Brazil.” Other programs spend several days in Argentine wine regions while focusing on Rio de Janeiro and Iguazu in Brazil.

## Argentine wine: two different areas to explore

**Mendoza and the Andean foothills.** [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) is a natural starting point for discovering wineries in Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley. On the [15-day “Argentina: from Iguazu to Patagonia” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/), separate days after Salta are devoted to wineries in both areas. The tour also visits Buenos Aires, both sides of Iguazu and southern glaciers. Tastings are therefore a substantial part of this specific itinerary, not just an incidental possibility.

Dedicated introductions to winemaking are offered on excursions in [Luján de Cuyo](/argentina/lujan-de-cuyo/lujan-de-cuyo-winery-tasting/) and the [Uco Valley](/argentina/uco-valley/uco-valley-winery-tasting/). Before choosing, compare their inclusions with the tour: winery visits, the number of tastings, lunch and transportation may differ. The name of a wine region does not establish a specific service package.

**Salta and Cafayate.** Northwestern Argentina offers a different experience: vineyards surrounded by dry mountain valleys, with gorges and historic towns that can be added along the way. The [private “Buenos Aires, Salta and Iguazu” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/buenos-aires-salta-iguazu/) includes a drive to Cafayate, a visit to a winery, a wine museum and an overnight stay in a wine hotel. It is a particularly good choice for travelers who want winemaking to be a meaningful part of a varied journey with other cities and natural stops.

Consider the location of these areas. Cafayate and Mendoza are not two suburbs of Buenos Aires: each requires a separate travel stage. If wine is the main reason for the journey, decide how many winery days you want before adding more countries.

## What happens in Brazil

In the itineraries in this selection, the Brazilian part usually passes through [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Rio introduces the city, its restaurants and culinary life, while the main program at Iguazu focuses on the falls. **A trip with all its tastings in Argentina or Chile should not automatically be presented as a Brazilian wine tour.**

Food-related interests in Brazil can be explored through specific restaurant visits, local dishes or workshops if they are actually included in the chosen program. Ordinary hotel breakfasts and a free evening for dinner are not standalone gastronomic excursions. If you are looking for a particular culinary format, ask us to show the day that includes it or discuss extending the itinerary.

One waterfall system lies along the border, but excursions on the Brazilian and Argentine sides are different. Allow time for [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), flights and border crossings regardless of your winery plans.

## A third country may be the most important one for wine

Several suitable multi-country tours continue from Brazil and Argentina to Chile. Wine valleys lie close to Santiago, and the [Maipo wine excursion](/chile/maipo-valley/maipo-valley-wine-tour/) is a separate product.

For example, [“Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama”](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/) visits Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago and the Atacama. But the word “wine” in the title alone does not specify which tastings are included. Check the daily itinerary and services section. On the [11-day New Year journey through Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-11-days-2027/), Maipo Valley can be added optionally; this is an activity in Chile, not a paid-for wine excursion in Argentina or Brazil.

On the [private 17-day journey through Chile, Argentina and Brazil](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/), wine days are divided between Chile and Mendoza in Argentina. This really does allow you to compare two national winemaking traditions in one trip. The itinerary is far longer than an ordinary weekend, as it also includes Easter Island, the Atacama, Patagonia and Iguazu.

## How to compare wine programs properly

| Detail | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Tasting or production tour | Different activities, sometimes arranged separately |
| Private or group visit | Guide arrangements, timing and conditions differ |
| Whether lunch is included | A winery ticket does not automatically include food |
| Transfers and travel | May take up a significant part of the day |
| Wine included or charged separately | Changes the actual budget |

It is especially useful to clarify which winery is visited, how much time is allocated, whether Russian-language guiding is available and how the return transfer is organized. On one tour, a winery is part of a main day; on another, it can be added on request. We distinguish these options before the booking is confirmed.

When planning several wine regions in different countries, account for regional flights, border crossings and possible restrictions on carrying purchased bottles. If Chile is on the route, rules apply for declaring products of plant or animal origin; check how purchased goods are treated under current customs regulations. Buying wine during an excursion and being allowed to take it across a border are separate questions.

## When to go and how to arrange the order

Argentina and Brazil cover vast territories with different climates. Weather in Mendoza or Cafayate's wine valleys differs from hot Rio and the humid surroundings of Iguazu. Seasonal priorities depend on whether you want to visit a winery during a particular stage of the agricultural year, see the waterfalls or combine the journey with a festival. There is no single best month for all these goals.

A sensible sequence depends on available flights and confirmed visits. For example, winery days in Cafayate can fit between Buenos Aires and Iguazu, while Mendoza may fall between northern Argentina and Patagonia. If tastings are in Chile, time is allocated around Santiago rather than portraying the Chilean activities as Argentine.

## Frequently asked questions about food and wine tours in Argentina and Brazil

### Do all suitable tours visit wineries in both countries?

No. Confirmed itineraries often place wine days in Argentina, while Brazil focuses on Rio and Iguazu. Sometimes the main tasting is actually in Chile, a third country on the route.

### Where should I choose a winery tour in Argentina: Salta or Mendoza?

For vineyards around Cafayate and the mountainous northwest, consider the [tour via Salta](/multi-country/tour/buenos-aires-salta-iguazu/). For dedicated days in Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley, the [Mendoza itinerary](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/) works better. These are different regions and should not be combined without extra days.

### Are dinner and tastings included in the price?

Services depend on the tour and specific excursion. Some programs include a tango show with dinner; on others, a winery is offered separately. Review the “Included” section and the conditions for each day.

### Can wineries be combined with Iguazu?

Yes. For example, the [private “Buenos Aires, Salta and Iguazu” tour](/multi-country/tour/buenos-aires-salta-iguazu/) combines the Cafayate wine program with the falls. The key consideration is the number of flights and total trip duration.

### Which should I choose if I only care about gastronomy?

Start with actual tasting and production days, then choose the geography. Compare [multi-country gastronomic routes](/multi-country/interests/food-and-wine/) and [wine tours in Argentina](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/argentina/).

## Nature in Argentina and Brazil: what to see on one journey

Our selection offers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring Argentina and Brazil as main destinations and a nature theme. **Some programs also pass through Chile, Uruguay or other countries.** The two-country filter identifies a required combination but does not limit the whole journey to those countries.

Most commonly, the countries are connected by [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), after which the route develops in one of two directions. One leads to southern Argentina and the [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), mountain lakes and Tierra del Fuego. The other leads to Brazil's [Amazon region](/brazil/place/manaus-amazon/), rivers and humid tropical forest. Your choice determines the climate, number of flights and character of the excursions.

For every type of cross-border journey, there is a [general Argentina + Brazil catalog](/multi-country/argentina_brazil/). Here we focus on the nature programs and their practical differences.

## Iguazu: why both sides of the falls are worth comparing

From the Brazilian bank near [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), visitors enjoy broad panoramic views of the cascades. On the Argentine side near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), a different network of walkways, bridges and viewpoints runs through humid subtropical forest. These are two national parks on opposite sides of an international border, both recognized by UNESCO.

Walking along one bank does not replace visiting the other. Allow time for border control, entry documents, transfers and each park's rules. High water and weather can temporarily affect access to individual trails, so check conditions for the actual excursion day.

On the [10-day Argentina and Brazil journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-brazil-10-days/), Iguazu is combined with cities and other natural attractions. The [12-day route with El Calafate and Ushuaia](/multi-country/tour/argentina-buenos-aires-el-calafate-ushuaia-iguazu-12-days/) adds Argentina's southern regions. The [journey with the Amazon, Iguazu and Buenos Aires](/multi-country/tour/brazil-amazon-argentina-manaus-iguazu/) covers a different geography.

The forests around Iguazu are rich in biodiversity, but a normal visit to the viewpoints does not guarantee sightings of particular animals. If you want to look specifically for wildlife, compare [Argentina and Brazil wildlife-watching tours](/multi-country/argentina_brazil/interests/wildlife/).

## Patagonia after Iguazu: glaciers and mountain lakes

When the journey continues from the falls to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), the scenery changes dramatically. Los Glaciares National Park is known for glaciers, lakes and mountains. The [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) can be seen from designated viewing platforms; ice walks and excursions on the water require specific inclusions and adherence to the operators' rules.

[Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/) introduces a different side of the Andes, with lakes, wooded slopes and mountain panoramas. Farther south, Tierra del Fuego offers colder winds and coastal landscapes. If the itinerary includes neighboring Chile, there may be an opportunity to visit [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/).

The [26-day Argentina and Patagonia program](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) is one example: it adds Bariloche, El Calafate, El Chaltén, Chilean Patagonia and Ushuaia to Iguazu. Compare it with the shorter [12-day option](/multi-country/tour/argentina-buenos-aires-el-calafate-ushuaia-iguazu-12-days/) according to time in each natural region.

Windy conditions in Patagonia can affect excursions even in the local warm season. Warm layers, wind protection and sensible buffers between long transfers are important. Not every nature attraction requires trekking: viewing a glacier and undertaking a multi-day mountain hike are different experiences.

## The Amazon after Iguazu: rivers and tropical forest

An alternative nature-focused route continues toward Manaus. On the [Brazil and Argentina tour featuring the Amazon](/multi-country/tour/brazil-amazon-argentina-manaus-iguazu/), the itinerary explores a tropical river region before returning to Iguazu and the Argentine capital. Look at the specific program for details of forest walks and boat outings: durations, transport and conditions differ.

The Amazon and the forests around Iguazu are different natural environments. In the Amazon's river areas, seasonal flooding and water levels shape much of the experience, while Iguazu's main attraction is its waterfalls, rocky banks and network of national-park trails. Walking conditions, insects, humidity and luggage needs are different.

Some excursions may include evening caiman watching or other encounters with animals. But such an outing must be confirmed in the individual tour; **wildlife sightings should not be promised on every nature-focused itinerary**.

## Choosing between the Amazon and Patagonia

| Nature priority | What to check |
|---|---|
| Iguazu | Both sides and the trails |
| Patagonia | Glaciers, wind and flights |
| Bariloche | Lakes and duration |
| Amazon | Boats, forest and seasonal water levels |
| Extended overview | Time spent in each region |

With limited days, consider allocating more time to Iguazu and just one additional natural region. Patagonia requires flights south; the Amazon requires a flight to the Manaus area. Longer itineraries can combine several regions but increase time spent in transit.

For small groups and independent travelers, we can coordinate flights, ground transfers, hotels and local guides. Changes are discussed in relation to a particular tour; a VIP label or high price alone does not guarantee a specific level of service.

## Weather, seasons and border crossings

Iguazu is warm and humid, with heavy spray near the falls. Patagonia is significantly cooler, especially in the wind. The Amazon remains hot and humid, but the conditions of river and forest excursions change with the seasons. **Choose dates around your main natural priority**, then check compatibility with other stops.

For Iguazu, quick-drying clothing and protection for electronics are useful. Patagonia calls for windproof layers and suitable footwear; the Amazon, for protection against sun, moisture and insects. If the itinerary spans several environments, check domestic-flight baggage restrictions in advance.

Crossing between Brazil and Argentina requires documents appropriate to each traveler's citizenship. Visa, transit, permit and medical requirements should be checked against current official sources before booking. Even when the national parks are close together, they are not one administrative territory.

For other combinations, see [nature tours in Argentina](/interests/nature/tours/argentina/) and [nature tours in Brazil](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/). If another region interests you, try the [general multi-country nature selection](/multi-country/interests/nature/).

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina and Brazil

### Can both sides of Iguazu Falls be visited?

Yes, if both excursions are included in the route. Check the days, transfers and border-crossing conditions between [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/).

### Which should I choose after Iguazu: the Amazon or Patagonia?

For river excursions and tropical forest, choose the Amazon. For glaciers, mountain lakes and southern landscapes, choose Patagonia. Compare travel distances and the days allocated by the tour.

### Is special preparation needed to visit a glacier?

The requirements for viewing platforms usually differ from those for walking on ice. Specialist ice excursions may have separate age and medical restrictions.

### Is a jaguar sighting guaranteed in the national park?

No. Jaguars may inhabit the forest, but a tourist walk never guarantees an animal encounter. Choose specially arranged wildlife excursions for that purpose.

### When is the best time to visit the two countries?

There is no single ideal period for Iguazu, Patagonia and the Amazon. Choose your principal natural region first, then compare its season with the other stages.
